title: What is Normalization?
question: What is database normalization? What problems does it solve?
realWorldScenario: Normalization prevents data anomalies (update/insert/delete anomalies) from corrupting the database.

title: First Normal Form (1NF)
question: What is First Normal Form (1NF)? Give an example of a table that violates 1NF and show how to fix it.
searchIntent: first normal form example violation fix
realWorldScenario: Storing multiple phone numbers in a single column violates 1NF.

title: Second Normal Form (2NF)
question: What is Second Normal Form (2NF)? What is a partial dependency and when can it occur?
realWorldScenario: An order-items table where product_name depends on product_id alone, not the composite PK (order_id, product_id) — that's a partial dependency.

title: Third Normal Form (3NF)
question: What is Third Normal Form (3NF)? What is a transitive dependency and how does it violate 3NF?
realWorldScenario: An employees table where department_name depends on department_id (not employee_id) — transitive dependency.

title: BCNF (Boyce-Codd Normal Form)
question: What is BCNF? How does it differ from 3NF and when does it matter?
realWorldScenario: Rarely tested at fresher level — advanced database theory.

title: When to Denormalize
question: What is denormalization? When would you intentionally denormalize a database schema?
realWorldScenario: Read-heavy analytics or reporting databases denormalise to avoid expensive joins on every query.

title: Update, Insert, Delete Anomalies
question: What are update, insert, and delete anomalies in an unnormalized database? Give one example of each.
searchIntent: insert delete update anomaly database normalization
realWorldScenario: Update anomaly: changing a department's location requires updating every employee record with that department.
